host_read.scratch_staging_disclosure: A FRESH process has no live integrations registry, so app.family_depth.default_channels() reads ENABLED_INTEGRATIONS from deploy-to-ec2.sh; that file is NOT on the host (deploy_script_on_host_opt=False). The scratch tree therefore carried the release tree's deploy-to-ec2.sh (byte-equal to the live base's; equals the release blob: True) beside app/, and the read's channel claim was 'inferred' by construction. The running service has a populated registry and does not read the file. The first attempt without the file raised FileNotFoundError (no AWS call made).

body.process_wide_state: The admin router now imports app.family_depth at process start (app/admin_api.py, the first added line) and the admin route table grows by ONE entry (measured on the host: 15 routes at the live ref, 16 at the candidate). READ, not instrumented: I opened app/admin_api.py (71 lines at trunk; the diff against the live ref is exactly the two added lines), app/family_depth.py (413 lines; its top level holds only the imports json, os, re, sys and datetime, string and path constants, one re.compile and a __main__ guard; boto3 is imported lazily INSIDE read(), so importing the module opens no client) and app/owner_gate.py (unchanged, already imported by admin_api). No logger, handler, signal, thread, socket, environment read, sys.path change or global-config change happens at import; the module-level objects are constants. The route's only effect at request time is read(): events.describe_rule, s3.get_object and s3.list_objects_v2 under the OG-cd-3 grant, run in the request threadpool, behind owner_gate.owner_only. Nothing here arms the probe listener or writes any parameter.
